title: Milieu Fragmente: Technologische und ästhetische Perspektiven
designer: Florian Lamm, Sascia Reibel (concept: Florian Lamm, Helmut Völter)

description.main: A German-language volume of essays on the concept of milieu as a way to describe technological and aesthetic environments. Edited by Rebekka Ladewig and Angelika Seppi, third in the ilinx. Kollaborationen series.
description.extended:
A collection of German-language essays that takes the biological notion of the milieu and asks what it can say about technological and aesthetic surroundings today.

Milieu Fragmente gathers contributions from philosophy of technology, cultural studies and art history. The editors propose an updated understanding of the milieu, a term that comes from the life sciences, and test it against artificial intelligence, data analytics and interconnected systems. The book was published by Spector Books in Leipzig in December 2020 as a thread-sewn softcover of 392 pages. Florian Lamm and Sascia Reibel designed it, with a design concept by Lamm and Helmut Völter. The cover names it as number 3 in the ilinx. Kollaborationen series.

Rebekka Ladewig and Angelika Seppi edit the volume. The publisher lists it in its Analysis&Excess series of the ilinx collaborations. Spector Books lists the title as out of print.

notes: Library holds 2 copies. Series: ilinx. Kollaborationen 3 (Spector Books lists it under Analysis&Excess). Publisher lists the title as out of print. Identified from a spine photograph; edition not checked against the copy.
